extracted.intended_audience: general readers and creators interested in feminist satire, online humor, and media culture
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and implicit standards for producing online feminist parody (site articles, headlines, books, podcasts) that mimic and critique women's media while remaining accessible, topical, and funny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the fake news actually funny
rubrics_metrics.description: "If you’re going to write fake news, you should make it funny" — the primary requirement for satirical pieces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor is the core objective: parody or mimicry alone is insufficient. Prioritize comedic payoff and the joke's clarity; pieces should be judged first on whether they make readers laugh or recognize a sharp satirical point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parody the voice and conventions of women's media
rubrics_metrics.description: Create pieces that are a parody of women's magazines and mainstream women's media, lampooning the way they "spoke to women."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mimic the tone, recurring phrases, and structural conventions of outlets like Cosmo or Teen Vogue so the satire reads like an exaggerated version of the original. Use that familiar voice as the target for critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame satire in the context of a woman's experience
rubrics_metrics.description: "We’re doing what we can to frame it in the context of a woman’s experience."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground jokes in recognizable female experiences and cultural touchstones; resonance with lived experiences increases comedic impact. Avoid abstractions—use specific scenarios that an intended audience will identify with.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep references accessible — avoid requiring specialist knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: "You don’t need a women’s studies degree to laugh..." — aim for broad accessibility rather than niche academic references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pop-culture and everyday cultural knowledge rather than dense theory. An accessible reference set widens audience and shareability; over-reliance on esoteric allusions can limit comedic reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use topical and pop-culture hooks
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply satire to current controversies and pop-culture moments (e.g., La La Land/Moonlight, Uber controversies, celebrity activism, conversations about sexual assault).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness enhances relevance and virality. Tie jokes to ongoing news cycles or well-known cultural moments to make pieces feel immediate and pointed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft headlines that mimic mainstream style while delivering the twist
rubrics_metrics.description: Headlines should read like the mainstream pieces being parodied (example: "Uber CEO Hires Psychic to Get to The Bottom of All The Bad Vibes in Here").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headlines are crucial: they should plausibly imitate the target publication's voice so the comedic inversion lands quickly. Balance plausibility and absurdity to maximize shareability and punch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend and maintain a consistent satirical premise across formats
rubrics_metrics.description: The site's satire can be extended into other formats (e.g., satirical self-help books, podcasts, speaking tours) while preserving the same 'bad manual' or magazine-editor premise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistency of persona/voice across media strengthens brand and comedic identity. When branching into books or podcasts, preserve the conceit so audience expectations are met and satire remains coherent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assemble contributors with strong comedic backgrounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Founders and staff come from improv, sketch, and other comedy writing backgrounds (e.g., Onion, SNL), which informs the site's voice and quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hiring writers and editors with live-comedy, sketch, or established satire experience improves joke construction, pacing, and editorial judgment. Contributor pedigree is a quality signal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage community safety and moderation to protect writers
rubrics_metrics.description: Reductress has banned comments to diminish harassment of writers, though they still face attacks on social platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Active moderation, comment policies, or disabling comments can reduce harassment and allow writers to do their work. Consider platform-level strategies to protect contributors from targeted abuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and mitigate misinterpretation as real news
rubrics_metrics.description: A common complaint is people misinterpreting satire as real news; this generates backlash from readers who think the pieces are genuine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that closely imitative satire risks being read as real; consider signals (tone, bylines, site framing) that clarify intent while accepting some trade-off between believability and clarity. Prepare PR/community responses for confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define and target a specific audience (resonance over universality)
rubrics_metrics.description: The site is explicitly aimed at American women who have been saturated with 'confidence-crippling messages' from women's magazines, seeking content that 'speaks to them directly.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor content to the lived experiences and cultural references of the intended demographic. Resonance with the target audience is more valuable than attempting to please all readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be adaptable to changing political/cultural climates
rubrics_metrics.description: Expect topical focus to shift with the sociopolitical moment; what you plan to satirize may change (e.g., from hypothetical female president commentary to older, recurring issues).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain flexibility in editorial priorities so satire remains timely and relevant; revisit recurring targets when they re-emerge in public discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue shareability and digital growth strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Reductress's viral headlines and social presence have produced quarter-of-a-million unique monthly visitors and Facebook virality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimize pieces for social platforms (memorable headlines, concise premises, culturally resonant jokes). Track analytics and platform behavior to inform what kinds of satire spread most effectively.
